From the implementation to orchestration at work

The AI increases the ability to produce faster than increases the capacity to verify and integrate what has been produced. Where this happens, human labor goes to depend more on specifying, checking, integrating and responding to the result, and gain net depends on how the organization reforms the review, metrics and governance.

Listening Guide

What to fix while listening

The table follows the audio order. The right column is the version that the evidence supports.

Twelve audio statements and the version that evidence supports
On audio What Evidence Sustains
"AI brain fry" caused a 33% jump in decision fatigue by the end of the day. In a Boston Consulting Group (BCG) survey with 1 488 US workers, who reported brain fry (about 14% of those using AI) reported 33% more decision fatigue than those not reported. It's a difference between groups, in a single moment. It doesn't measure increase throughout the day or cause proof.
Dopamine peaks "when a person tries hard at something uncertain," and AI "zeros the biological equation." Dopamine signals the difference between the reward received and the expected. No study measured dopamine during the use of AI. The connection with the effort and the AI is speculation.
"Research calls this the illusion of thought," speaking of projecting humanity into a chat. It's two different things. Assigning understanding to a program is the ELIZA effect (Weizenbaum, 1966). "The Illusion of Thinking" (Apple, 2025) deals with the limits of puzzle reasoning models, and was challenged.
Developers type code 55% faster. In an experiment, who used GitHub Copilot finished a task (an HTTP server) 55.8% faster. It doesn't measure typing or real work. In another experiment, with 16 developers experienced in projects they knew, AI tasks took 19% longer.
"The net delivery speed drops to 0.85 times the original." No source with this number was found.
Conway's reverse maneuver is "the solution MIT addresses." Conway's reverse maneuver comes from the practice of consulting (ThoughtWorks) and the book Team Topologies. No MIT proposal was found.
"Intrinsic, Germanic and extrinsic" charges. The terms of cognitive charge theory are intrinsic, pertinent (germane) and strange (extraneous). The theory comes from teaching; applying it to teams is an adaptation.
Science "destroys the myth" of brainstorming without judgment, and evaluating during generation is superior. The brainstorming Group It yields less ideas than the same people alone. But no study shows that evaluating during generation is always better. The order between generating and evaluating depends on the task.
The "banking case study": credit approval agent, 98% threshold, 0.25 margin, zero hallucinations, latency −92% and cloud cost −78%. It's the benchmark. offline the author of this site (Case Agents): 30 service consultations, simulated tools, without credit and without production. Router threshold is 0.75, not 98%. The minimum relative margin is 0.25. There were 0 incorrect executions in 20 queries; hallucination was not measured. The 77.8% is the reduction in the cost of calls to the model, not the cost of cloud. The latency was not measured.
"They evaluated 150 multi-agent executions with Cohen Kappa of 0.88, confirming failure patterns." In the MAST study (UC Berkeley, 2025), 150 tracks served to create taxonomy, and 0.88 measures the agreement between human annotators. The study found 14 failure modes and failure rates from 41% to 86.7% in seven systems.
DeerFlow 2.0 "purchases real computers for AI to use the mouse"; Sompo has "10,000 agents operating daily". DeerFlow 2.0 (ByteDance, February 2026) runs agents in containers with browser and terminal; no source talks about renting computers. Sompo has announced AI agents for around 30 mil employees, with pilot from January 2026; no source confirms the number of agents quoted in the audio.
The EPOCH framework of MIT combines stoicism, Taoism, Confucianism and Bushidō, and charges "empathy, presence, authentic opinion and constructive hope". Epoch is MIT Sloan (2025). It has five groups: empathy, presence, opinion and judgment, creativityAnd hope and leadership. No source links Epoch to the philosophical traditions cited. The link is an analogy of the author.

The automatic transcription misgraphed some names ("MOSCO", "Matriz-Ghout", "CRIBE", "HAG", "Cloud Mythos"). Transcription of this page uses MoSCOW, GUT matrix, CRIB, RAG and Claude Mythos, who is Claude Mythos Preview of Anthropic. The full list is in search log.

Critical review

What the Evidence Shows

Each block has a seal: fact is a result reported by the source; inference combines results; hypothesis There's still not enough validation.

Fact

1. The AI accelerates defined tasks, and the gain varies

In controlled experiments, AI reduced time and improved quality in writing, service and consulting tasks. In a call center with 5 179 attendants, cases solved per hour increased 14% on average and 34% among novices, with minimal effect among the most experienced. With 758 consultants, the gain appeared within what the model does well; otherwise, the correct answers fell by 19 percentage points.

Sources: Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond (2025); Noy and Zhang (2023); Dell'Acqua et al. (2025).

Inference

2. Producing more does not guarantee to deliver more

Data from more than 10 000 developers show more pull requests with AI, 91% longer revision and no correlation with delivery at the organization level. The DORA search (DevOps Research and Assessment) of 2024 associated more adoption of AI the small drop in flow and stability of deliveries. The two results are correlated: they do not prove that AI caused the change. An alternative explanation is that bigger changes, not the AI itself, slow down the review.

Sources: Faroes AI (2025); DORA (2024).

The line changes places. When writing gets faster and review does not stay, the work accumulates in the review.

Fact, with exception

3. Supervising AI costs

The literature on human factors describes, since 1983, that automating the easy part leaves the person the difficult part, with less practice, and that those who supervise automation tend to trust them too much. In 2026 BCG researchers named it AI brain fry the mental fatigue of those who use or supervise AI beyond their own capacity.

Sources: Bainbridge (1983); Parasuraman and Manzey (2010); Bedard et al. (2026).

Fact, with small samples

4. Delegating can reduce learning

In an experiment with 52 programmers, those who used AI to learn a new library scored 17 points lower in an understanding test, with no significant time gain. Whoever used the AI to ask and understand kept the note. In four colonoscopy centers, the detection rate without AI fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after months of AI use. The two studies are small, and the second is observational.

Sources: Shen and Tamkin (2026); Budzyń et al. (2025).

Fact

5. Agents advance, but tests show limits

The size of tasks that agents complete with 50% success doubled every about seven months between 2019 and 2025, but performance falls into unstructured tasks. In a simulated office, the best agent completed 30% of his chores alone. Systems with various agents failed in 41% to 86.7% of the executions analyzed.

Sources: Kwa et al. (2025); Xu et al. (2025); Cemri et al. (2025).

Hypothesis

What this evidence supports from the audio thesis

Together, this evidence supports a part of the audio thesis: the neck changes place, and with it the human role. They do not support the other: that change is already general, that it reduces human effort or that it releases the mind to grow. Labour market data show, so far, small effects on average (Denmark, 25 000 workers) and concentrated effects on young exposed occupations (USA).

Sources: Humlum and Vestergaard (2025); Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen (2025).

Explanatory model

Three scenarios

The result depends on the conditions. The indicators of the third column help to know what scenario a team is in.

Scenarios, conditions and observable indicators
Scene When it's plausible How to Recognize
Favourable: AI increases effective productivity and releases time Tasks the model does well; automatic tests; small changes; people who use AI to understand, not just to delegate Flow and stability rise together; revision time does not grow; performance without AI remains
Intermediate: execution accelerates and revision absorbs part of the gain Manual review; major changes; activity goals (lines, tickets, points) More pull requests and same delivery; longer review
Adverse: errors, dependency and supervision cancel the gain Tasks outside what the model does well; excessive trust; little practice without AI Stability drops; serious errors increase; performance without AI falls

Inference The software data from 2024 and 2025 are more similar to the intermediate scenario. This can change with new tools.

Range

What this page does not affirm

  • It does not say that orchestration will replace execution in all professions. Almost all studies are software, writing and attendance.
  • You don't say "orchestrator" is a new profession. It is a combination of known competences: specify, review, coordinate and respond to the decision.
  • You don't use the philosophical traditions of audio as evidence. They are analogies of the author.
  • It does not treat company ads as proof of output in production.
  • Models change faster than research. The studies cited used tools from 2023 to 2025.

In short

What audio hits and what needs correction

The AI increases the ability to produce faster than the ability to check. Where this happens, human work depends more on specifying, checking and responding to the result. Net gain is not guaranteed.

  • Gain with Limits — experiments show gains in defined tasks, higher for novices; outside of what the model does well, performance falls.
  • The line changes places — observational data show more code and longer revision, without visible gain in delivery of the organization.
  • Supervision costs — complacency with automation, reported fatigue and loss of practice have evidence, with small samples.
  • Fixed numbers — the "case banking" of audio is an offline benchmark of the author; the drop in delivery cited has no source; the 33% is difference between groups.

Full record: 56 statements audited, with sources and gaps.

Frequently Asked Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Has the AI moved the execution work to orchestration?

Partly, and only in a few contexts. Experiments show gains in delimited tasks, and software engineering data suggest that the bottleneck passes for review. Labour market data have so far shown small effects on average and concentrated effects on young people from exposed occupations. There is no study that directly measures orchestration work.

What is AI brain fry?

It is the name that BCG researchers gave in 2026 to the mental fatigue of those who use or supervise AI tools beyond their own capacity. In a survey with 1,488 US workers, who reported the problem reported 33% more decision fatigue than who did not. The research shows association, it doesn't.

Does AI make developers faster?

Depends on the task and the person. In an experiment with a short task, the group with Copilot finished 55.8% faster. In an experiment with 16 developers experienced in projects they knew, AI tasks took 19% longer.

Does AI harm learning?

It can hurt when the person only delegates. In an experiment with 52 programmers, those who used AI to learn a new library had a lower score in an understanding test. Whoever used the AI to ask and understand kept the note. The sample is small.

What does the study of multi-agent system failures say?

The MAST study by UC Berkeley classified flaws in 14 modes and 3 categories and found failure rates from 41% to 86.7% in seven open source systems. The Kappa value of 0.88 measures the agreement between human annotators.
